integrationVerdict.reason: The harness directly invokes the registry and consumer and constructs a URL in memory. It does not execute subscribeToIosNativeCallEvents, IosNativeCallsBridge readiness or cold-start drainage, Expo Router replacement, the mounted thread effect, or an external system URL through Linking and redirectSystemPath. It is not equivalent to the required local integration chain.

phase1Ci.reason: Full CI is prohibited until all current Level C lanes report P0=0/P1=0; this current review records three open P1 findings.

findings.summary: The correction made external startCall/openCall text inert by deleting the thread consumers, but retained legitimate in-app producers. Inbox and profile Voice/Video shortcuts still navigate with startCall, and the communication compatibility route still navigates with openCall=1; the thread no longer consumes either intent, so those authenticated foreground product actions silently degrade to ordinary navigation.
evidence: app/chat/index.tsx:287-300 and 383-415 still produce startCall from user-visible inbox and people-search Voice/Video actions
app/profile/[userId].tsx:1623-1628 still produces startCall for profile Voice/Video actions
app/communication/[roomId].tsx:36-43 still produces openCall=1 for the compatibility redirect
app/chat/[threadId].tsx contains no requestedCallMode/autoStartCallRef or requestedOpenCall/autoOpenCallRef consumer

scripts/proof-chilly-chat-end-to-end-call-initiation.mjs:65-71 requires startCall producers but lines 108-115 reject every thread consumer, allowing the proof to pass while the requested transition is no longer exercised
docs/release/CHILLY_CHAT_END_TO_END_CALL_INITIATION_PROOF.md documents that startCall triggers the requested call and docs/PUBLIC_V1_READINESS_CHECKLIST.md documents openCall compatibility behavior
findings.impact: A security correction regresses legitimate authenticated internal Voice/Video entry behavior and weakens its end-to-end regression proof. This is product behavior loss in the reviewed domain, not merely a documentation mismatch.
findings.requiredResolution: Preserve external route text as navigation-only while introducing a trusted memory-only foreground navigation intent or another reviewed internal authority for legitimate UI producers; add mounted end-to-end tests that prove the UI action reaches exactly one call start/open without letting copied URLs reproduce it.

findings.summary: The claimed repository-wide sole-creator guard matches only the literal function name followed by an opening parenthesis. A production module can import the creator under an alias or invoke it through a computed namespace member and remain invisible to both the focused test and policy guard.
evidence: scripts/test-ios-native-call-route-provenance.mjs:75-93 scans each line with /registerTrustedIosCallKitNativeEvent\s*\(/
scripts/guard-ios-native-call-policy.mjs:27-40 uses the same literal-name regex
a valid aliased import and call left the detected callsite set unchanged at only app/_layout.tsx:1127
a valid namespace import with provenance["registerTrustedIosCallKitNativeEvent"] left the detected callsite set unchanged at only app/_layout.tsx:1127
the extra-creator mutant appends a bare exact-name call to an uncompiled source string and therefore does not exercise import binding or valid production compilation
findings.impact: The production-wide creator allowlist and the authority-boundary anti-vacuity claim are not proved. A future untrusted URL, screen, or notification module could acquire the creator under a different binding without failing the gate.
findings.requiredResolution: Use an AST/import-binding-aware scan or structurally restrict creator acquisition, and add compilable alias-import, renamed-destructuring, namespace-member, and computed-member mutants that the real gate rejects.

findings.summary: No simulator app launched, and the substitute harness does not execute the real bridge-to-router-to-mounted-thread path. It directly calls claim creation and consumption helpers, bypassing the lifecycle and routing boundaries whose behavior it is offered to replace.
evidence: docs/assurance/d2c-ios-native-action-route-provenance-report-v1.json records simulatorAppLaunched=false
scripts/test-ios-native-call-route-provenance.mjs directly calls registerTrustedIosCallKitNativeEvent and consumeTrustedIosCallKitNativeEventClaim and constructs a URL in memory
the harness does not execute subscribeToIosNativeCallEvents or IosNativeCallsBridge auth/readiness and cold-start event drainage
the harness does not mount Expo Router and app/chat/[threadId].tsx to exercise router replacement, claim parsing, effect ordering, and one-time consumption
the harness does not invoke an external custom scheme or Universal Link through the actual Linking and redirectSystemPath entry points
findings.impact: IOS_NATIVE_ROUTE_PROVENANCE_LOCAL_INTEGRATION_CLEAR cannot be accepted, and the owner-required simulator-or-equivalent merge gate remains open.
findings.requiredResolution: Execute the required simulator path, or provide a reviewed local mounted integration harness that uses the actual native subscription adapter, auth readiness/cold-start drainage, Router replacement, thread consumer, and external URL adapters without directly bypassing those components.

findings.summary: The committed source report still describes a pre-freeze and pending-review state after correction and synchronization, and states that ordinary notification sensitive parameters and fragments are stripped although the in-app notification router path is not sanitized.
evidence: docs/assurance/d2c-ios-native-action-route-provenance-report-v1.json state remains LOCAL_GENERATION_COMPILE_AND_EQUIVALENT_INTEGRATION_PASS_PENDING_FREEZE
the same report leaves T1/T2 pending and lists immutable source commit and base synchronization under remainingBeforeFreeze
the report says ordinaryNotification=SENSITIVE_CALL_PARAMETERS_AND_FRAGMENTS_STRIPPED, while components/notifications/notification-bell-button.tsx routes resolved application paths directly
findings.impact: The report overstates route normalization and is not an exact synchronized-head account, although route-only transition authority is independently denied by the current thread policy.
findings.requiredResolution: Publish additive exact-head evidence and distinguish stripped external system URLs from in-app navigation paths that are safe because route text has no transition authority.

findings.summary: The iOS native-intent hook now removes the entire fragment from every system path, while the application-link parser intentionally merges fragment parameters for password recovery and auth callbacks. No focused executable regression proves that initial recovery/auth links still reach the canonical auth listener with their required fragment values.
evidence: app/+native-intent.tsx:12-14 sends every iOS system path through sanitizeExternalIosNativeCallPath
_lib/nativeCallTransitionProvenance.mjs:248-260 clears parsed.hash unconditionally and strips fallback input at either query or fragment
_lib/appLinks.ts:136 and recovery/auth route handling intentionally merge fragment parameters
the independent application-links proof could not run in the clean review worktree because the local TypeScript dependency was unresolved
findings.impact: This is an unclosed adjacent regression risk for authentication/recovery routing; it is not classified as a reproduced product defect at this head.
findings.requiredResolution: Add executable initial and live auth/recovery fixtures with fragment-carried values and prove the canonical auth listener receives them while native-call claim fragments remain stripped from navigation and analytics.
